newsitem.title: USA: US March S&P 500 futures rally late to end higher.
newsitem.headline: US March S&P 500 futures rally late to end higher.

text.p: March Standard and Poor's 500 futures rallied late to end up and near session highs, buoyed by a recovery in technology and blue chip stocks.
March S&Ps tested support at several points during the session, stumbling as low as 782.90 as Treasury bonds began the first leg of this week's quarterly refunding.
But traders said support at 783.00 basically held, with short-covering and a rebound in the tech sector rescuing sluggish S&Ps.
"Does this give us enough fuel to test the 800 level? I think it does," an S&P 500 trader said.

"We've been sitting here treading water while the tech sector has fallen apart," he said of recent action in the Nasdaq and S&P 500. "The S&P has held in," he said. March Nasdaq 100 hit a one-month low before recovering today.
"Now if the tech sector has put in a bottom today, that should give us the fuel to get to 796.00 and even hit those stops at 97 and get to 800," he said.
Still, others noted that the four forays above 796.00 since the contract high was set January 23 have failed.
Traders pegged resistance at 796.60 and the record high of 799.70, and support remains at 785.80 to 786.00.
Traders estimated March S&P 500 volume Tuesday at 84,000, with a hefty portion of that seen in the afternoon, they said.
Traders said buying from four or five firms was featured late.

"We had a lot of buying from (a dealer), the OTC market came back, and we definitely held to some extent yesterday," an S&P technician said. "I think we'll see some new contract highs very soon," he said.
Traders were keeping an eye on T-bonds for direction as well, especially before 10-year and 30-year auctions this week.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 6.80 at 794.85, Value Lines were 3.95 higher at 706.45, NYSE Composites were 3.65 higher at 416.70, Nikkeis were 100 higher at 18,210, Midcap 400s were up 0.60 at 263.70 and Nasdaq 100s were up 7.25 at 881.75.
